title: A Cliff Made of Glass
before: 读前先二选一：游隼搬进城市，是它适应了城市，还是城市刚好合它的老规矩？
带着这个判断读，留意文章在哪一段给出答案——通常是一句很短的话。
paras: Forty floors up, on a narrow ledge of a bank tower, a peregrine falcon stands still. Below it the street runs like a grey river. The bird is not lost. This is home.

Sixty years ago this scene would have been impossible in most of eastern North America. The birds had almost disappeared, and the cause was not hunting or the loss of wild rock. It was a pesticide sprayed on fields. The poison moved up the food chain and built up in their bodies. It made their eggshells thin, so thin that they broke under the weight of the parent that sat on them. Few young survived. By the 1960s the eastern population was gone. The species was listed as endangered, and the chemical was banned.

Then came the strange part. Scientists raised the birds in captivity and looked for places to put them back. A nesting bird needs three things: a ledge high above the ground, open air in front of it, and a steady supply of birds flying past. Rock had offered all three for thousands of years. But good rock is rare and far apart, and the young kept failing in the same old places.
Someone looked at a city and saw the same three things. A skyscraper has high shelves. It has open air. And it has pigeons.

The falcons did not adapt. This is the part most people get wrong. Adaptation means a population changing over generations: new behaviour, new limits, a body that slowly fits a new problem. These birds brought their old rules with them. A bird that had never seen a building still chose a high ledge with open air below, because that is what its species had always chosen. The city taught it nothing. The city simply had the right shape. The word for this is preadaptation: a feature that evolved for one job turns out to fit another, and the animal can move in without changing at all.

Notice how different this is from the singers in the last article. City birds that sing higher had to shift their song, generation after generation, until the traffic stopped drowning them out. They changed. The falcons only arrived.

Today they nest on bridges, churches and apartment blocks. In some regions the cities now hold more pairs than the rock the species came from. They thrive there: prey is abundant, the concrete holds heat, and most ground predators never get near the nest. But a cliff made of glass has its own bill. Young birds crash into windows at speed. And when territories sit close together, as they do downtown, sickness passes quickly from neighbour to neighbour.

Still, the bird is a good reminder that a city is not only a place that forces animals to change. Sometimes it is a place that happens to look like home. The cliff was in the bird all along; the glass only had to imitate it.
after: 一句话主旨：两句话以内。
圈 3 个词：最挡路的，或者看着眼熟但说不准的。点一下就是圈了。
三句复述：一句概括、一句细节、一句你的判断（同意不同意，为什么）。
note: 第 5、6 段是全文的转折：前面讲「出了什么事」，后面讲「所以这说明什么」。作者从故事切到道理的地方，往往只有一句短句，而且常带否定或转折。第一遍别停在词上，先把这个切口找到。
